evidence.note: Maintained a rolling running checklist in Plan prose, consistently re-stating which modules/templates/static files were done vs remaining (database→config→utils→oauth→api→ui→main→templates→css/js→start.sh), giving a roughly accurate done-vs-remaining picture.

Ran broad subsystem verification across the surface — OAuth token flow, favourite, boost, notifications, lists, bookmark, reports, polls, trends, security headers, hashtag/404/unauth pages — demonstrating usable coverage tracking of many subsystems, though not an explicit gate-by-gate ledger.
Detected the stuck/circular state promptly and repeatedly — correctly diagnosing an unterminated database.py heredoc consuming all commands — so it clearly noticed being stuck (above anchor 3).

Despite continuous detection, it looped the same diagnosis/recovery for ~140 steps without time-boxing or successfully redirecting, consuming most of the horizon on one issue — falling short of the level-8 'recognizes thrashing and time-boxes it' behavior.

Final status account is mostly accurate (all files built, database.py corrupted) but slightly over-optimistic ('built and tested successfully'); it retains an accurate picture of what exists and what broke.

reasoning: During the build the agent kept a usable running checklist of subsystems and tested a broad slice of them, matching the level-5 anchor (roughly accurate view of what remains). It also detected the circular/stuck heredoc state immediately and persistently, clearing anchor 3's 'doesn't notice until much later.' But it never converted that detection into time-boxing or an effective redirect — it thrashed on the same issue for the majority of the horizon — and never maintained an explicit granular verified-vs-pending ledger of the full gate/endpoint set, so it does not reach anchor 8. Level 5 best fits.
